blocks.text: CASE STUDY // PRIVATE CLIENT
An AR mobile experience built for a private real estate client, letting buyers scan a surface and walk through a full building, down to a single apartment, before it's ever built.
Solo Design & 3D Direction
3-Week Sprint
Client Concept-to-Demo Build
Designed end-to-end by Neha Mayacharya while at CXR.Agency (now Kinemeric)

images.alt: Ascension Realty title slide with cityscape graphic

blocks.text: A private real estate client approached CXR.Agency with an early-stage idea: use AR to let clients and investors experience their developments virtually, from anywhere in the world. The concept was promising but rough — no clarity, no structure, no defined user journey.
The Ask
Scan a surface, walk from a city skyline into one apartment: city → tower → floor plan → room, as one continuous journey.
The Constraint
Three weeks, start to finish, with a five-person team and no existing app to reference.
The Challenge
No onboarding, no walkthrough — it had to read clearly the first time someone picked up a phone.
I owned concept, storyboard, asset direction, UX, interaction design, and sound — the next slide breaks this down.
With the Creative Director's approval and the 3D/dev teams' build support, every other decision on this project ran through me — concept through to final testing.

contributions.name: Storyboarding
contributions.body: Created the scale-by-scale journey storyboards that defined the city-to-room experience.

contributions.name: Asset Curation & Optimization
contributions.body: Sourced 3D models from TurboSquid and optimized them for real-time AR performance.

contributions.name: Interaction & UX Design
contributions.body: Designed the entire app journey with gestures, transitions, and room-level navigation.

contributions.name: Holographic Shader Direction
contributions.body: Art directed the UI shading blending behind the AR scan in HoloKit.

contributions.name: Prototyping
contributions.body: Built click-through mockups in Figma to stress-test interaction before any dev handoff.

contributions.name: Sound Design
contributions.body: Designed the audio layer, ambient tone and interaction feedback across the experience.

contributions.name: Developer Sync
contributions.body: Partnered directly with the two-person dev team to get every interaction functioning as singles.

contributions.name: Testing & Iteration
contributions.body: Tested builds across devices and wrote concise notes into the design system.

blocks.text: Four principles carried the concept from a one-line brief into a scene-by-scene experience — each shows up directly in the storyboard and flow on the next two slides.

goals.name: Narrative Journey
goals.body: Guide the user through an abstract yet emotionally coherent story of ascension, literally rising from a city skyline down into a single home.

goals.name: Minimal UI, Maximum Impact
goals.body: Design interactions that feel organic to a 3D space rather than a 2D app squeezed into AR — the space itself does most of the talking.

goals.name: Sensory Immersion
goals.body: Blend sound, light, space, and touch into one seamless experience, so the tour feels physical even though nothing in it is real.

goals.name: Speculative Interaction Design
goals.body: Explore how someone might naturally interact with an intangible, spatial transition — there was no existing app to borrow patterns from.

sections.label: 05 / Concept & Storyboarding

blocks.text: Eleven sequential wireframes worked out frame-by-frame before a single 3D asset was constructed.
The storyboard serves as the design contract. With no preexisting platform references, shot-by-shot planning was vital for the 3D team to build precisely scaled assets.

moments.name: Splash to scan
moments.body: The experience opens in the real world, not a menu — before anything digital appears.

moments.name: City to tower to floor plan
moments.body: Three deliberate zoom-in moments carry the 'ascension' narrative forward smoothly.

moments.name: Pinch and proximity together
moments.body: Zoom is both a manual screen gesture and a physical side-effect of moving closer.

sections.label: 06 / UX Flow

blocks.text: If the storyboard shows what the user sees, this is the logic underneath it — the six-stage path from opening the app to standing inside one room, and the four gestures that move someone between stages.

stages.name: Landing
stages.body: Start — open the AR app on mobile or tablet.

stages.name: Onboarding
stages.body: One instruction, no tutorial screens: "Scan a flat surface to begin."

stages.name: World Build
stages.body: A 2D city grid appears, then extrudes into a full 3D cityscape.

stages.name: Selection
stages.body: Pulsing icons mark available units; tapping one zooms into that tower.

stages.name: Interior
stages.body: The floor plan extrudes into a 3D interior the user can zoom into.

stages.name: Room Focus
stages.body: Tapping a room label surfaces its details, then explore more or end.

triggers: Pinch gesture — zooms the 3D interior in or out.
Tap pulsing icon — selects a unit from the cityscape.
Tap room label — jumps to Bedroom / Kitchen / Living Room, etc.
Avatar walk — a 3D figure animates into the selected room, cueing the camera move.

blocks.text: Three problems shaped nearly every design and technical decision on this project — each of them needed a design answer before a single line of Unity code could solve it.

challenges.name: Plane Tracking
challenges.body: Buildings and floor plans had to land correctly on the user's real surface — level, stable, and walkable, with no drifting or re-centering needed.
challenges.solution: I defined multiple Vuforia anchor points so the experience could snap cleanly between city view, tower, and apartment without losing tracking on the handoff.

challenges.name: Building Scale
challenges.body: The models needed to read at full scale while staying detailed, without forcing the user to keep walking around to see everything.
challenges.solution: Assets sourced from TurboSquid were re-scaled and optimized by hand, and zoom acted as scale — proximity to the device stood in for physically walking closer.

challenges.name: Full Cityscape
challenges.body: Showing the development in the context of a real city made it far more convincing, but building a whole city risked doubling the workload.
challenges.solution: Surrounding structures were kept as low-detail blockouts with a holographic materialize shader, so only the actual development needed full modeling fidelity.

blocks.text: Three moments carry the entire experience — each one is a deliberate escalation of detail, from a full building down to a single, well-lit room.

features.name: Full Models
features.body: Using the device's camera, 3D buildings instantly materialize in the user's own space, giving an immediate sense of a development's true scale before stepping any closer.

features.name: Furnished Floor Plans
features.body: A tap transports users inside the building to navigate a fully furnished 3D floor plan, exploring each room with real layouts and furniture in place.

features.name: Unobtrusive Details
features.body: Property and room information lives in a details panel beside the viewfinder, designed to inform without ever crowding the 3D experience itself.

images.alt: Apartment details panel showing Unit 2300 with furnished interior

blocks.text: Vectary let me test scale and interaction in physical AR space with a mobile device before any of this went to Unity — faster iteration, more informed decisions, before handoff to development.

blocks.text: A functioning platform and a sample project the client could put in front of real prospects, turning a rough idea into proof that AR belongs in real estate marketing.
With a functioning platform and a sample project to showcase, the client is ready to build out the use case and change the way shoppers approach real estate.

results.name: Functioning Platform
results.body: A working mobile AR app, not just a concept deck, ready to demo end to end.

results.name: Client-Ready Demo
results.body: A sample project the client's team can put directly in front of prospects.

results.name: Tenant-to-Investor Utility
results.body: Built for the full range of real estate shoppers, not one narrow use case.
